title: The arc: seven things sought in the bath, and whether they are stages
md:
**How to read it.** Each number links to the claim behind that sentence and the page it quotes.

Native terms: *temazcalli* (Nahua sweat house), *pyria* (Greek vapour bath), *loutron* (a wash, a bath), *balaneion* / *balneum* (bath-house), *thermae* (the great public baths), *tevilah* (immersion) in a *mikveh* (a gathering of undrawn water), *hammam* (bath-house), *'awra* (the parts of the body that must be covered), *snana* (bath) at a *tirtha* (ford, holy bathing place), *sveda* (induced sweating), *wenquan* 溫泉 (hot spring), *muyu* 沐浴 (washing hair and body), *misogi* 禊 (washing off defilement, *kegare*), *balneum Mariae* (the alchemists' water bath).

## 1. The made heat is a person

The Nahua sweat house is somebody. In Sahagún's Book 6 the midwife says to heat the bath, "the flowery house of our lord", and let the girl enter "our mother" [[1]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#am-sahagun-midwife-heat-the-bath-our-mother); the Nahuatl column has *xochicalli*, flower house, and "our common mother, the grandmother, Yoalticitl" [[2]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#am-sahagun-nahuatl-flower-house-grandmother), and where the friar's Spanish says "goddess of the temazcalli" the Nahuatl says "grandmother of the temazcal", who lies and keeps watch there [[3]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#am-sahagun-nahuatl-grandmother-of-the-temazcal). Householders set her image on the bath [[4]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#am-sahagun-temazcalteci-image-on-the-baths); Durán reports a small stone idol buried under each new one [[5]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#am-duran-god-of-the-baths-buried-under) and tore baths down to find it [[6]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#am-duran-had-baths-torn-down); a figure at the door took copal from the sick [[7]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#am-magliabechiano-advocate-of-illnesses-at-the-door). Heat does the work: a weak fire only gives a headache [[8]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#am-sahagun-nahuatl-weak-heat-only-headache).

The other made-heat baths are described from outside and carry less of this. Herodotus' Scythians cleanse themselves after a burial in a felt tent with red-hot stones, howl, and use it "instead of a *loutron*" [[9]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#nor-herodotus-scythians-cleanse-after-burial) [[10]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/pleasure#nor-herodotus-instead-of-a-bath). The chronicle's Apostle Andrew sees Slavs beat themselves with twigs in wooden baths, "washing, not torment" [[11]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/company#nor-karamzin-nestor-andrew-wooden-baths) [[12]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/company#nor-karamzin-nestor-washing-not-torment). Latvian women healers cure in the bath-house and a bride throws money into it [[13]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#nor-einhorn-women-cured-in-the-bathhouses) [[14]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#nor-einhorn-bride-throws-money-into-the-bathhouse). Charaka's *jentaka* is a domed sweat-house by a pond with a charcoal oven, entered with a blessing and a warning that a man who leaves the bench and cannot find the door may die [[15]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/building#ind-charaka-jentaka-house) [[16]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#ind-charaka-jentaka-warning). Al-Ghazali makes the hot room a likeness of hell [[17]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#isl-ghazali-hot-room-is-like-hell).

**Verdict on stage 1:** holds for Mexico, on the Nahuas' own words. For the Scythians, Slavs and Latvians the sources show a rite and a place that receives offerings, not a person.

## 2. The found water has an owner

Pliny says it outright: healing springs "increase the number of the gods under various names and found cities" [[18]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#rom-pliny-springs-add-gods-found-cities). Minerva presides over Britain's hot springs, with a fire that never whitens into ash [[19]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#rom-solinus-britain-springs-minerva); a curse was dropped into that spring with coins from Vespasian to Constantine [[20]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#rom-bath-curse-tablet-found-in-hot-spring) [[21]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#rom-bath-curse-tablet-melt-like-water). The cured drop silver and gold into Amphiaraus' spring [[22]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#gr-pausanias-amphiaraus-spring-coins). At Mount Li one sacrificed three victims before entering, and the spring was the gift of a goddess who had first spat sores onto the First Emperor [[23]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#chn-lishan-three-victims-before-entering) [[24]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#chn-lishan-goddess-spat-on-first-emperor). Izumo's spring is "the gods' hot water" [[25]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#jpn-izumo-fudoki-gods-hot-water). The pilgrim asks the Ganga's pardon for touching her with his feet [[26]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#ind-padma-ganga-apology-for-feet). An angel stirs Bethesda [[27]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#scr-bethesda-angel-troubles-water). In 1618 a Latin poet still gives a German spring a *Numen*, a Genius who punishes drinkers, and Nymphs [[28]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#spa-fautsch-numen-in-the-spring) [[29]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#spa-fautsch-genius-of-spring-against-revellers) [[30]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#spa-fautsch-nymphs-guard-the-sour-spring). The foundation legends of the Bohemian spas give the discovery to animals: a hound at Karlsbad, pigs at Teplitz [[31]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#spa-karlsbad-hunting-dog-legend) [[32]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#spa-schwenckfeld-teplitz-found-by-pigs).

**Verdict:** the best-attested stage, in every region read.

## 3. Physicians take the water from the god

They do, and they disagree. Hippocrates ranks water from ground with hot springs or metals as bad [[33]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#gr-hippocrates-hot-spring-waters-bad); Vitruvius says all hot water is medicinal because it is cooked in what it passes through [[34]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#rom-vitruvius-hot-water-medicinal); Pliny sorts Baiae's waters by sulphur, alum, salt, nitre and bitumen [[35]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#rom-pliny-baiae-kinds-of-water). Ibn Sina reduces the bath to heating by air and wetting by water [[36]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#isl-ibn-sina-bath-heats-by-air-wets-by-water); Charaka lists what *snana* does and thirteen ways to sweat a patient [[37]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#ind-charaka-snana-benefits) [[38]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#ind-charaka-thirteen-sveda); Zhang Heng's hot spring carries off pestilence when the six *qi* are disordered [[39]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#chn-zhang-heng-hot-spring-rhapsody); the Tlatelolco physicians prescribe the *temazcalli* for contracted sinews, late pregnancy and after childbirth [[40]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#am-sahagun-book11-all-the-sick-benefit) [[41]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#am-sahagun-tlatelolco-physicians-gave-the-account). The god is not evicted: Galen calls Asclepius his ancestral god [[42]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#gr-galen-asclepius-ancestral-god-saved-him). One story has the physicians evicting the spring: at Tiberias a king pulled down the healing rooms "so that people should not do without physicians" [[43]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#isl-muqaddasi-king-pulls-down-healing-rooms). Paracelsus denies Pfäfers is heated by earth-fire and makes it grow and die with the herbs [[44]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#spa-paracelsus-pfaefers-not-from-earth-fire) [[45]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/transformation#spa-paracelsus-pfaefers-rejuvenates-with-the-herbs); Montaigne found no miracle and no harm [[46]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#spa-montaigne-no-miraculous-effect).

## 4. Purity becomes a law with measures

Leviticus requires "living water" [[47]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#scr-leviticus-living-water); a 1346 code says drawn water is invalid and rainwater valid [[48]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#jew-dura-mikveh-rainwater-not-drawn); a 1687 Amsterdam prayer book converts forty *seah* into 5,760 eggs and 192 beer measures [[49]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#jew-aboab-forty-seah-in-amsterdam-beer-measure), and nothing may stand between flesh and water [[50]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#jew-womens-sermon-nothing-between-flesh-and-water). The Garuda Purana ranks waters up to the Ganga and separates clean limbs from the "fruit" of a *tirtha* [[51]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#ind-garuda-ranking-of-waters) [[52]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#ind-garuda-water-cleans-body-tirtha-gives-fruit); the Skanda Purana does arithmetic with it [[53]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#ind-skanda-bath-merit-arithmetic). Izanagi judges the current before his *misogi* [[54]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#jpn-kojiki-middle-current-and-gods-of-pollution). Daoist texts prescribe the decoction, the room and the day [[55]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#chn-yunji-bamboo-and-peach-bath-after-defilement) [[56]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/building#chn-bath-room-kept-from-latrine-well-stove-altar) [[57]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/transformation#chn-yunji-bathing-days-and-hours). Al-Ghazali's rules are about eyes, intention and feet, not water [[58]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#isl-ghazali-bath-duties-of-the-eyes) [[59]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#isl-ghazali-bath-intention-fee-left-foot). Aristophanes' patient is washed in the sea before the night in the precinct [[60]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#gr-aristophanes-plutus-sea-bath-first).

## 5. The city bath is company and pleasure, and the moralists answer

Seneca above the *balneum* [[61]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/company#rom-seneca-ep56-lodges-above-bath) [[62]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/company#rom-seneca-ep56-sounds-of-bath); Martial on Nero's *thermae* [[63]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/pleasure#rom-martial-nero-and-his-thermae); Baghdad's five thousand baths, pitch-black cubicles and three towels [[64]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/company#isl-yaqubi-baghdad-five-thousand-baths) [[65]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/building#isl-ibn-battuta-baghdad-baths-pitch-and-towels); a free endowed bath in Khorasan [[66]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/company#isl-qazwini-free-bath-in-khorasan); the daily crowd "as at a market" in Izumo [[25]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/cult#jpn-izumo-fudoki-gods-hot-water); the floating table at Baden [[67]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/company#spa-poggio-floating-table-no-german); Montaigne's view that the company is the best part of the cure [[68]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/company#spa-montaigne-company-best-part-of-effect). The answer is the same in six languages and is mostly about who sees whom: Seneca on Scipio's dark bath and Baiae [[69]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#rom-seneca-ep86-old-baths-for-use) [[70]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#rom-seneca-ep51-baiae-luxury); Tacitus [[71]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#rom-tacitus-baths-part-of-servitude); the Rites' "men and women do not share the bath-room" [[72]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#chn-liji-men-and-women-do-not-share-bath-room); the Companions' "good house, evil house" [[73]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#isl-ghazali-good-house-evil-house); Ibn Battuta having contracts drawn up over waist-wrappers [[74]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#isl-ibn-battuta-minya-contracts-for-waist-wrappers); the friars on the *temazcalli* [[75]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#am-tudela-many-offenses-in-the-heat) [[76]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#am-duran-never-bathed-without-the-other-sex); Olaus Magnus correcting Poggio [[77]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#nor-olaus-sexes-parted-by-boards-against-poggio). Durán's remark cuts the other way: for the Nahuas bathing without the other sex was a bad omen. Rank divides the water too: an "official pool" and a "mixed pool" at Mount Li [[78]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/company#chn-lishan-official-pool-and-commoners-pool).

## 6. The inner bath answers the outer

Every purity tradition read has the voice. Jeremiah: natron does not wash iniquity [[79]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/critique#scr-jeremiah-natron-does-not-wash). Mark sets washings against the heart [[80]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/critique#scr-mark-washings-and-the-heart). Al-Ghazali calls outward purity the husk [[81]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/critique#isl-ghazali-outer-purity-is-the-husk). A Madhyamaka treatise argues that if water removed wrongdoing the blind and lame who bathe at the fords would be cured [[82]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/critique#ind-tengyur-if-water-removed-sin-none-would-suffer) and quotes against the brahmins a verse the Hitopadesha also carries: the self is the river, bathe there [[83]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/critique#ind-hitopadesha-self-is-the-river) [[84]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/critique#ind-atma-nadi-verse-shared-by-buddhist-polemic). The Padma Purana itself says a pilgrim worrying about home loses the fruit [[85]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#ind-padma-ganga-bath-needs-the-mind). A Daoist scripture defines two baths, an empty heart and a clean body [[86]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/purity#chn-yunji-inner-and-outer-clean); Zhu Xi reads King Tang's basin as washing the heart [[87]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/transformation#chn-tang-basin-inscription-zhu-xi). Fautsch: "do not, with washed feet, pile up filth in your breast" [[29]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/morals#spa-fautsch-genius-of-spring-against-revellers). Naaman's objection is the outsider's form of it: why this river [[88]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/critique#scr-naaman-rivers-of-damascus).

## 7. The bath as a figure of transformation

Amaterasu is born from the washing of an eye [[89]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/transformation#jpn-kojiki-amaterasu-born-from-washing-left-eye). Naaman's flesh returns "like the flesh of a small boy" [[90]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#scr-naaman-wash-seven-times), and the alchemists take him over: copper seeks the "bath of regeneration" seven times in the Jordan [[91]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/transformation#alch-clangor-naaman-bath-of-regeneration). Immersion returns the soul to its place [[92]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/transformation#jew-shelah-immersion-returns-the-soul). The laboratory's *balneum Mariae* is a real tub with a copper pipe [[93]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/building#alch-brunschwig-balneum-mariae-in-a-bath-tub); the Rosarium washes the black body with dew [[94]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/transformation#alch-rosarium-ablutio-dew-washes-the-black-body); Splendor solis boils an old man young [[95]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/transformation#alch-splendor-solis-old-man-cut-up-and-boiled). Peter Martyr reports the rejuvenating spring and declines to believe it; a tract of 1700 makes him vouch for it [[96]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/transformation#alch-martyr-boiuca-fountain-doubted) [[97]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/transformation#alch-communication-1700-martyr-made-to-assure).

## Verdict on the hypothesised arc

**The seven are not stages.** In every region where more than a handful of pages were read, at least five of the seven appear together, and in the oldest layers as readily as the latest: the Kojiki has law (the right current), a person-like water and a birth in one scene; 2 Kings 5 has cure, rite, the sceptic and rebirth in fourteen verses; Sahagún's Book 6 and Book 11 have the grandmother and the physicians in the same codex.

**What does change is who holds the pen.** Physicians write stage 3, jurists stage 4, moralists and travellers stage 5, and the bath's own people are heard directly only in the Nahuatl column, the Kojiki, the Purana's prayer and the Bath tablet. Where the sources are outsiders (Scythians, Slavs, Latvians, the Inca baths), stage 1 and 2 thin out, which says more about the witnesses than the bathers.

**Where the texts break the hypothesis.** (a) "Heat is a person" is specifically Nahua in what we hold; elsewhere it is the water that has an owner. (b) Physicians do not agree that hot springs are good: Hippocrates and Olaus Magnus [[98]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/medicine#nor-olaus-no-natural-hot-baths-in-the-north) think them harmful. (c) Mixed bathing is not only a scandal: for the Nahuas (per Durán) it was required. (d) The alchemical bath is less a bath than a fire: the Rosarium rejects the *balneum Mariae* for dung [[99]](/explore/histories/bath/claims/transformation#alch-rosarium-bath-of-mary-not-the-right-fire).

**One practice or several?** Several, sharing a room. The one thing common to all of them is that nobody in these sources treats getting into hot water as a neutral act: it needs a reason, a rule, a payment, a companion or an apology.
